description.narrative: Along with at least nine other Caritas member organisations, CAFOD made a contribution towards an appeal issued by Caritas Thailand for emergency relief to poor and vulnerable people, including both Thais and migrant workers, living in the Archdiocese of Bangkok and the Diocese of Nakhonsawan, who were affected by severe flooding. 11 relief centres were set up to provide services to people able to reach them, and also to serve as a base from which relief workers could deliver supplies (by boat if need be) to more isolated communities. The main relief plans comprised provision of 30-day ration package including drinking water, rice, cooking oil, noodles, salt and canned fish to 11,000 households, together with water purification tablets and filters. 3,000 of these households, in particularly isolated locations, would receive supplementary items. 110 health volunteers would be trained to support and complement the work of the Thai Red Cross and the government's public health system by disseminating information on disease control to an estimated 44,000 people in 56 communities, and in the process picking up any complicated health situations and arranging to refer them to the health services. These volunteers, and other Caritas staff in the relief centres, would also provide psycho-social support to flood-affected families by providing opportunities for people to receive support and counselling. Temporary work would be provided for 2,500 flood-affected farmers through which they could earn vouchers exchangeable for foodstuffs and other essential items in local markets. Caritas also planned to provide cash grants to ten savings groups so they could advance small loans to help people do whatever they needed to get back to normal as quickly as possible.
